claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 17, I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar courses), or in approved training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in college or anything like that. He left school and isn't doing any courses at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Let me ask a couple more questions to fully assess your situation.

Is Alex registered with a careers service, a government training programme, or similar organisation? For example, in England this would be a "qualifying body" that provides careers advice or training support for young people.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't signed up with anything like that. He just left school and went straight into work.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 17 and is no longer in full-time education, approved training, or registered with a careers service/qualifying body, I need to check the eligibility rules to give you an accurate answer.

Let me review the official guidance to confirm the details.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the official guidance I've reviewed, I now have the information needed to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's what I found:

- Child Benefit normally continues if a child aged 16 or over stays in **approved education or training**
- You can apply for Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- Child Benefit **stops** if your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training

Just to confirm one final detail: Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's working full-time at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to make a decision on your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

- **Alex is 17 years old** – For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit normally only continues if they remain in approved education or training.
- **Alex is not in education or training** – He left school and hasn't enrolled in any approved courses.
- **Alex hasn't registered with a careers service** – If he had registered with a government-sponsored careers service (or the armed services), you could have claimed for an additional 20 weeks after he left education.
- **Alex is working full-time** – Under the rules, Child Benefit stops when a child over 16 works 24 hours or more per week and is no longer in approved education or training.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future – for example, if he decides to return to approved education or training – you may become eligible again. If you have any questions or want to discuss your situation further, you can contact the Child Benefit Office.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news, but I hope this helps clarify your situation. Is there anything else I can help you with?
